And on her watch armed attacks and murders have increased dramatically. Armed attacks by 70k. We ask how is infighting and factionalism impacting your safety?

Press Release:


Riah Phiyega Hits Back
Police watchdog, the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) has recommended that suspended police commissioner Riah Phiyega and two senior officials face criminal charges for their role in the Marikana massacre. She hit back saying it’s just a witch-hunt to damage her reputation and she has done nothing wrong. What will the future hold for the embattled commissioner?


Script:



Riah Phiyega Backlash Script


VO: 6
National Police Commissioner Jackie Selebi – suspended and later jailed on corruption charges in 2010

VO: 5”
His successor Bheki Cele - mired in controversy and sacked in 2012

VO: 7”
Riah Phiyega – suspended last November and facing an inquiry instituted by President Zuma on her fitness to hold office….

All 3 personally appointed by the incumbent president at the time says Institute for Security studies – Gareth Newham.

Gareth:
And so for the last 3 National Commissioners the individual holding that post has simply not been the person of the kind of caliber in terms of integrity that we need to ensure that an organization the size of the police service can do the work it needs to do.

Bongani link
There have been a number of investigations involving officials at the most senior level of our security organisations. It’s a high stakes game in which the players don’t know who is friend or foe and one in which every move could be your last.

VO:
IPID this week recommended to the NPA that Phiyega be charged with defeating the ends of justice for her role in the Marikana saga says acting national spokesman Robert Raburabu.

Robert:
She would be charged in relation to contraventions of the protection of information act.

VO:
Phiyega was having none of it.

Phiyega press conference:
The undignified haste to announce my immenent charging smacks of a sustained concerted effort by the people and entities in the police ministry to continue with a relentless campaign that seeks to harass, slander and vilify me.

Robert:
This is not like a personal vendetta against the commissioner. Its not directed at any individual. Its an investigation that needs to be carried out because of what happened.

Phiyega
I have not been approached by IPID to be apprised of my charges or at least to give a warning statement. I truly believe that my rights as a citizen are being violated.

VO: 9”
But with no operational experience - her appointment was a poisoned chalice.

Gareth:
Suddenly somebody who knows nothing is telling you what to do. I think that is where at various stages she started to feel insecure and she started sidelining some of the more serious and honest officials so we started to see a fracturing at the top of the organization.

VO: 21
Just 2 months into her tenurs Fractures that first manifested in the tragic massacre at Marikana that haunts us today. It’s widely held that the killings are a result of her inexperience and the guidance of political masters. Andries Nkoma is a lawyer representing the victims.

Andries:
She has on her own tried to hide the inputs of political heavyweights in this.

VO: 13”
At the Farlam Commission of enquiry into the death of 34 miners Phiyega spent 21 days on the stand – her performance under cross examination put her credibility and motives under the spotlight.

Gareth:
Her testimony before the Marikana commission was generally seen as evasive, dishonest and was designed to conceal rather than reveal.

VO:
The commission revealed 4 credibility issues – in the main she’d lied to the public of South Africa.

Initially she filed a report to the president saying that there were 2 separate incident with 17 mine workers killed in each.

Gareth:
After that letter she then released a public statement before the media saying that 34 miners were shot dead in one scene.

VO: 3
She also denied that there was ever a review process.

Gareth:
Later they uncovered a letters from her asking people to attend a review.

VO: 6:
She lied about when the decision to go tactical was taken.

Gareth:
She said that was taken around 13hoo on Thursday the 16th of August however later minutes showed that the decision was taken on Wednesday the 15th of August at a national management forum meeting which she was chairing.

Andries:
It simply says that she testified trying very hard to protect people who were her masters in the political space I believe.

Phiyega:
I did not lie and I am not a criminal.

VO: 30
Phiyega has played the game and been at the centre of several controversies. In 2012 IPID head at the time, Robert McBride wrote a damning letter to the police minister recommending an investigation into a 60 million rand Kwazulu natal supply chain misappropriation saga which found corruption in the highest echelons of the provincial police service. At the centre of the saga an alleged corrupt relationship between Provincial police commissioner Ngobeni and controversial local businessman Thoshan Panday. The Hawks’ General Johan Booysen led the investigation says journalist and author Barry Bateman.

Barry:
Thoshan Panday and senior police officers were accused of fraud worth about 60 million rand worth of accommodation fraud over the 2010 world cup. This was investigated by members under the command of General Johan Booysen.

VO: 27
The investigation found:

Panday paid for Ngobeni’s husband’s surprise birthday bash when she had been aware that he was under investigation.

• That Panday’s companies bid against one another to secure police contracts and tenders, to give the appearance of a competitive process.

• That Panday spent nearly R150 000 in gifts and favours for Supply Chain Management Unit cops

• Panday’s companies made a combined 200% profit on the police deals

Barry:
Now the dockets were compiled, the information was obtained and it was presented as a case to go to trial.

VO: 9”
Despite IPID boss McBride making recommendations to Riah Phiyega against the top cops involved – she then launched her own parallel investigation.

Barry:
It got to the point where McBride sent a letter to police minister Nathi Ntleko where he set out his concerns that Riah Phiyega was ignoring IPID’s investigations – she wanted to conduct her own investigation.

VO:
In effect subverting the investigation.

Barry
So serious did he find her failure to act that he recommended that she herself be suspended and hauled before a commission of enquiry on charges of misconduct, racketeering and corruption itself.

Gareth:
If you are a police officer and you come to knowledge of a crime you have a legal if not moral duty, obligation to act. To enforce the law, so that she did not do that raises questions once again of her integrity and her character.

VO: 17
And instead of waving goodbye to Provincial Commissioner Ngobeni at the end of her contract Riah Phiyega retained her despite the cloud hanging over her head.
As for General Booysen who tried to expose the situation – he found himself fighting for his career.

Barry:
He has faced almost every step from police management to get him out of the Hawks.

VO: 7”
First Booysen was suspended and linked to the Cato Manor death squad the charges were later deemed invalid and unlawful.

Barry:
He was then hauled before a disciplinary matter that was initiated by Riah Phiyega - he was cleared there.

VO: 6
And when that failed new charges were brought against him.

Barry:
This time related to allegedly fraudently obtaining a claim for a reward for a job well done dated back to 2008.

VO:
Booysen lashed back and took the matter to court.

Barry:
Not only was he re-instated by the judge but the judge assessed the merits of the particular allegation against Booysen and there was found that there was no case and remains on suspension. That matter is again being appealed and Booysen remains on suspension.

Gareth:
Clearly it was a campaign because he has won almost every court battle against the police.

VO: 21
Phiyega’s career has been marred by other scandals too. The ministerial reference group appointed by Police Minister Nathi Ntleko found Phiyega guilty of fraud, perjury and misconduct. The report was the culmination of a probe into allegations by senior managers alleging that Phiyega was involved in dodgy human resources practices.

Gareth:
SAPS is a very well regulated organization. It has to be because police officials are trained to have more powers than ordinary citizens and they carry fire arms. And if they make mistakes people die.

VO: 5”
It’s been alleged she refused to co-operate with this probe.

Gareth
She refused to co-operate with that Ministerial reference group and instructed other people not to co-operate with it. So not only did she know about it but she used the opportunity that was provided to her at the time to

VO: 13”
Adding to the list of public embarrassments was her tipping off of General Lamoer – Western Cape Provincial police commissioner alleged to be at the centre of a corrupt relationship with Cape Town drug dealer and businessman Salim Dawjee.

Gareth:
She initially told him that he was being investigated which was a breach of confidentiality – it was a top secret crime intelligence investigation.

VO:
It’s not just hearsay he says – there’s proof.

Gareth:
There is a transcript of her informing him. That is against the law.

VO: 15”
With this litany of scandals and investigations pinpointing the commissioner – you have to wonder why IPID has ignored the more damning evidence in favour of a minor contravention.

Barry:
It’s now she has served her purpose I suppose and she is on her way out and this is simply the mechanism to do it.

VO: 4”
Phiyega simply sees herself as a scapegoat and that’s why IPID is recommending the charges.

Phiyega presser
I am therefore saddened that such a tragic event continues to get used as a witch hunt against me and others for inexplicable and undeclared personalized vendettas.

Gareth:
Riah Phiyega is not a scapegoat. She is being held accountable for the errors that she committed. Dishonesty that she was involved in while she was the national commissioner of police. If she has evidence that others have committed crimes or that she is being used unfairly then she must provide that evidence to the public so we can all understand who is behind this campaign.




Promo 1:


VO: 7
Suspended police commissioner Riah Phiyega is fighting fires on all fronts - saying she’s a scapegoat.

Gareth:
She is not a scapegoat…dishonesty that she was involved in.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Promo 2:

VO: 15”
Riah Phiyega is facing a raft of serious allegations questioning her fitness to hold office. In a shock move this week the independent police investigative directorate recommended the top cop be charged with defeating the ends of justice.


Promo 3:

VO: 6”
We’ve had 3 consecutive national police commissioners disgraced. This week Riah Phiyega hit back.

“I am not a liar or a criminal.”
